round_interpretation: Round two increased hypervolume by 11.92%. Adding oil alone to the pruned no-lag rate model improved aggregate IC, NLL and Sharpe; IC and NLL improved in all three seeds, Sharpe in one. The seven-input oil/rate front has IC 0.311111, NLL -2.639529 and Sharpe 0.553264. Removing acceleration from the rank-free credit model produced a five-input front with lag and higher Sharpe 0.597448. Lag removal from the reduced density model raised IC/Sharpe in every seed with a small NLL cost; adding lag to the pruned rate model hurt IC/Sharpe in every seed despite improving density. The final family round tests oil/rate pruning, credit/oil bridges, exact lag contrasts on the changed parents, and one annual-momentum transfer.
default_expected_tradeoff: Report all three objective deltas, per-seed effects and calibrated interval diagnostics. Lag usefulness remains context-dependent; do not use a density improvement as a veto against IC/Sharpe gains.
default_falsification: A dominated result does not support the proposed conditional simplification or addition. The bounded family cap is a stopping budget, not proof that the retained inputs are universally necessary.
